summary: Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Henry Hoenigswald, and Zellig Harris. He served as assistant professor at Pennsylvania (1946–1989) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society (1964–1988).
Ernest Clerc de Landresse was an early scholar of Sinology and Japanology who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (~1820–1832) and at the École des chartes (~1828–1830).

Ernest Fenollosa worked in philosophy, Japanology, and art history after studying at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of the Arts, and was curator at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Ernest Herbert Cooper Walsh was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and history who studied at Trent College and University College London. He served as Lecturer in Bengali at Oxford (1920–1921) and Lecturer in Tibetan at SOAS (~1923–1930).

Ernest John Henry Mackay worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at the University of Bristol and under Flinders Petrie and John Marshall. He served as Custodian of Antiquities in Mandatory Palestine (1919–1922) and Special Officer for the Archaeological Survey of India (1926–1931).
Ernest Monnington Bowden was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who was educated at Malvern College (~1873–1878) and Pembroke College, Cambridge (~1878–1881).
Ernest Paxton Janvier was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his A.B. at Princeton University (~1912–1916) and his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania (~1916–1920).

Ernest Philip Horrwitz was an Indologist who served as Sanskrit Professor at Trinity College Dublin (~1909–1914) and Sanskrit Instructor at the City College of New York, alongside lecturing on comparative philology at the universities of Mumbai and Rangoon.

Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, linguistics, and history. Educated at Saint-Sulpice and the Collège de France under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère, he held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and as professor and director at the Collège de France.

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He held major professorial posts at Brown University from 1964 and Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

Ernst Arbman was an Indologist and scholar of religion who earned multiple degrees at Uppsala University under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and Jarl Charpentier. He became a docent at Uppsala in 1922 and Professor of Comparative Religion at Stockholm University (1937–1958).
Ernst Arthur Voretzsch was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology who studied law at the University of Göttingen from ~1888 to 1891.

Ernst Carl Büchi was an anthropologist and Indologist who earned Ph.D. degrees from the University of Zurich under Otto Schlaginhaufen and the University of Copenhagen. He served as Superintendent of the Anthropological Survey of India (1950–1958) and professor at FU Berlin (1966–1979).

Ernst Cassirer was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Marburg. He held posts at Berlin, the University of Hamburg (1919–1933), the University of Gothenburg (1935–1941), Yale University (1941–1944), and Columbia University (1944–1945).

Ernst Cohn-Wiener was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University. He taught at the Humboldt-Akademie (~1908–1933) and served as Director of the Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery (~1934–1939).

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He was a professor at Göttingen (1855–1867) and Humboldt University of Berlin, and served as director of the Altes Museum (~1872–1896).

Ernst Fraenkel was a linguist who studied at Bonn, Leipzig, and Berlin under August Leskien, Johannes Schmidt, and Wilhelm Schulze. He served as professor at Kiel University (1909–1936) and later lectured at the University of Hamburg (1945–1953).

Ernst Förstemann worked in linguistics and history, studying at Berlin and Halle under Karl Lachmann, Franz Bopp, and August Friedrich Pott. He served as librarian at Wernigerode and director of the Saxon State and University Library Dresden (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who habilitated at the University of Vienna (-2013). He taught at the University of Vienna (2006–2016) and has held research and leadership roles at the University for Continuing Education Krems since 2007.

Ernst Gombrich was an art historian who studied at the University of Vienna. He worked at the University of London (1956–1959) and spent his career at the Warburg Institute, where he started in 1936 and served as director from 1959 to 1976.
